content:
alex: Kicking off ORD GPU cluster bootstrap. Primary network goals: TGW attachment + route propagation, NAT/egress strategy for GPUs, private hosted zone delegation. Need handoff checklist and cost tradeoffs.

sam: Copying checklist I used in SFO with updates for TGW quotas. Will drop preflight steps.

pri: Quick note — ORD has a TGW attachment limit per account. Confirm we have spare attachments or request quota now (takes 24-48h). Also check route table propagation isn't blocked by explicit propagations.

maria: Cost angles: NAT Gateway per-AZ vs centralized NAT instances. For GPU workers (heavy model pulls) egress could be tens of TB/mo. Recommend estimate: NATgw ~ $0.045/GB + per-hour gw cost, might be cheaper to route heavy pulls through a cost-optimized egress VPC with reserved bandwidth.

leo: For validation, run these from a staging GPU node after bootstrap:
```
# check route to model registry
curl -I http://models-internal.redwood/artifact/metadata
# check resolver
nslookup api.internal.redwood ord-vpc.corp-hosted-zone
# check TGW routes
aws ec2 describe-route-tables --filters Name=tag:Name,Values=ord-tgw-rt
```

alex: @pri opened a quota ticket earlier today (case 123456). If that doesn't clear, fallback is per-VPC TGW attachment with shared transit and route table split. That complicates failover though.

sam: Preflight I added:
- Confirm TGW state `available` and peering attachments in `available`
- Ensure route propagation enabled on attachment routes
- Validate IPAM allocations for worker subnets (no overlap)
- Provision NAT Elastic IPs and verify EIP limit
- Create Private Hosted Zone delegation record in corp-zone

pri: Important: Route propagation showed race on initial attach last time — wait 60s, then `describe-transit-gateway-route-tables` to confirm routes. If missing, re-run `create-transit-gateway-route` against attachment.

maria: Egress firewalling: we should avoid per-request proxy for model downloads (adds latency). Allowlist artifact hosts in NACLs and use prefix-list for model CDN. Also track estimated monthly egress in the cost tracker: https://billing.internal/redwood/ord-egress (internal link).

leo: Handshake steps for DNS:
1) Create private hosted zone `ord.internal.redwood`
2) Create inbound Route53 resolver endpoints in ORD VPCs
3) Add forwarding rules to central resolver; test with `dig @10.0.0.2 some.internal.rdwd`
4) Add delegation records to `corp.internal` for `ord.internal`

alex: Ops-bot: create runbook checkpoint for ORD network handoff.

ops-bot: Runbook created: https://runbooks.internal/ord-network-bootstrap. Checkpoint ID rb-ord-2026-03-17-09. :white_check_mark:

sam: Smoke tests to run post-handoff (do all from a GPU node and from a control-plane instance):
- curl model registry (200)
- curl license server (200)
- push large artifact to S3 via presigned URL (simulate model upload)
- run long-lived download for 10GB to validate throughput and NAT billing paths

pri: If TGW route propagation fails and we need quick fallback: create explicit static routes per route table for the peer CIDRs pointing to the TGW attachment ID. Documented in the runbook.

maria: FYI — ORD has a soft limit on EIP per-region. If we plan per-AZ NAT gw, request an EIP quota bump or allocate a small pool ahead of time.

leo: After handoff, I will add a per-route monitoring dashboard: latency to model registry, egress bytes by AZ, NATgw error rates. We'll use that to tune batching/KB-cache behavior.

alex: Thanks all. Plan: sam to complete preflight by EOD, pri to confirm TGW quota ticket status, maria to post cost estimate, leo to publish smoke tests. Handoff tentatively tomorrow 14:00 UTC.

sam: On it.

pri: TGW quota approved (case 123456 -> approved).

maria: Uploaded egress cost calc to the billing tracker. Link in runbook.

leo: I'll be on the handoff call.

alex: Great. Adding this to the deployment calendar and tagging Platform Eng to collect rollback play. :thumbsup:
